sections.skill: Sort costs into one-time and recurring and convert periods

questions.prompt: Which is a one-time cost?

choices.text: Renewing the business license every year
Buying a used oven to start a bakery
Paying for a website hosting plan each month
Paying the monthly rent for the bakery space

questions.correct_answer: Buying a used oven to start a bakery
questions.intro: Business costs come in two timing types. A ONE-TIME (startup) cost is paid once to get going: equipment, a first batch of supplies, a state filing fee, or a website design. A RECURRING cost repeats on a schedule: rent, software subscriptions, insurance, phone service, or a yearly license renewal. To compare them, convert recurring costs to the same period, such as per month or per year. In this course, all prices in questions are example assumptions, not real market prices.
questions.feedback: Equipment bought once to start is one-time.

questions.prompt: How many months are in a year?
questions.intro: A year has 12 months. To turn a monthly amount into a yearly amount, multiply by 12. To turn a yearly amount into a monthly amount, divide by 12. Example: 25 dollars a month is 25 x 12 = 300 dollars a year, and 240 dollars a year is 240 / 12 = 20 dollars a month. Check: the yearly number should always be bigger than the monthly number.
